An icon set drawn from the horizon and the sail

Line icons made for this site only. They share the mark’s tilted horizon and its curved sail, the 2 px weight of the current interface icons, and one solid shape each, which can take the site blue. Every course, every theory article and every boat spec gets its own sign.

Four rules

Keep to these when you add an icon, and the set stays one family.

{{use:pin}}

24 grid, 2 px line

Drawn in a 24 px box with 2 px of air on each side, round ends and joins. Shown at 20 px in text and 16 px in fact chips, like the icons on the site now.

The horizon tilts

Wherever the sea meets the sky, the line rises 8.4° to the right, as in the mark. It is the thread that ties night sailing, buoyage, the ocean course and the language globe to the logo.

The curved sail

Sails keep the mark’s curved leech instead of a flat triangle. It is what makes the boats read as Ocean Way and not as a stock icon.

One solid shape

At most one filled part per icon: the sail, the day, the port light. Set --ow-2 to the accent for a two-tone icon; leave it unset for one colour.

The set

Each tile shows the icon at 48, 20 and 16 px, its id in the sprite, and where it belongs on the site.

Solid parts in the accent, or in the line colour.

What replaced the old icons

The site used a generic i-* sprite until November 2026; these are the swaps. Brand icons (Telegram, Instagram, YouTube, Threads) are kept, now part of the same sprite.

How to use

Paste icons/ow-icons.svg once at the top of the body (the prototypes already do this with their own sprite), then point at an id. Single files for Figma or the Next.js app are in icons/svg/.

<svg class="i"><use href="#ow-clock"/></svg>6 days

/* two-tone: solid parts follow --ow-2, the line stays currentColor */
.skills .i { --ow-2: var(--accent); }
